title: The Client Connector trusted network object and its v1 API
aliases: trusted network create returns no id

prose.text: A trusted network is a named, reusable set of detection criteria that forwarding profiles select as predefined trusted networks. The v1 API under `webTrustedNetwork` is in the generated surface; this subject holds its behavior.

prose.label: What it is for.
prose.text: Defining criteria once and selecting several networks in a profile: [[zpa.trusted-networks.zcc-relationship:zcc-defines-criteria]]. How the app evaluates them is [[zcc.trusted-networks.detection]].

prose.label: Criteria are strings.
prose.text: Each criterion is one comma-separated string: [[zcc.api.trusted-networks-wire:v1-criteria-strings]]. {{go-omitempty}}

prose.label: Condition type.
prose.text: {{condition-type-int}} The sources disagree on its wire type [[zcc.api.trusted-networks-wire:condition-type-wire-type]], and which code means All is only partly settled {{gap:condition-type-values}}, by the provider mapping in [[zcc.terraform.trusted-network-backend:v1-condition-type-mapping]].

prose.label: Listing.
prose.text: Both SDKs unwrap an envelope the contract does not show: [[zcc.api.trusted-networks-wire:list-envelope]], [[zcc.api.trusted-networks-wire:v1-list-shape]]. {{name-lookup-pages}}

prose.label: Create and update.
prose.text: Create and edit answer with a status only: [[zcc.api.trusted-networks-wire:mutation-response]], read as [[zcc.api.trusted-networks-wire:error-code]]. {{update-needs-id}} {{python-sends-kwargs}} The Python create's result therefore has no ID: [[zcc.sdk-python.return-shapes:add-result-has-no-id]]. The Go SDK's name lookup after create, and its blind sleeps, are in [[zcc.terraform.field-fidelity:trusted-network-create-sleeps-blindly]].

prose.label: ZPA link.
prose.text: {{zpa-id}} The provider calls it a ZPA tenant identifier, so do not read it as a per-network ID that matches ZPA's trusted network records, which are described in [[zpa.trusted-networks.zcc-relationship]].
What `active`, `guid` and the audit fields guarantee is open {{gap:metadata-semantics}}.

checks.do: When listing trusted networks directly, unwrap `trustedNetworkContracts` and page until a short page.
After a create or update, re-read the record: the mutation response carries only a status.
Treat `errorCode` "0" as success, not as a failure flag.
Before reading All or Any from a v1 `conditionType`, whether the code has been checked against the console for that tenant.

go-omitempty.statement: The Go SDK omits `ssids` and `trustedEgressIps` from a written body when they are empty, while it always sends the other criteria, empty or not.

condition-type-int.statement: The trusted network's `conditionType` sets how its own criteria combine; the Go SDK sends it as an integer with no omitempty, so 0 is always sent.

quotes: `condition_type` (String) — Match policy across the criteria below.

name-lookup-pages.statement: The Go SDK's lookups by name and by ID page through the list 1000 at a time until a page comes back short, comparing names exactly.

update-needs-id.statement: Update is a PUT to `edit` with the ID in the body: the Go SDK refuses to send an update without an ID, and the Python SDK sends whatever keyword arguments it is given without checking for one.

python-sends-kwargs.statement: The Python SDK's add and update send the caller's keyword arguments, with keys camel-cased by the request executor (apart from a set of snake_case keys kept for web policies), rather than the model's full field set, so unset criteria are absent from the body rather than sent empty.

zpa-id.statement: The Terraform provider documents that the API also returns a linked ZPA tenant identifier, `zpaId`, populated lazily (absent from the create response, present on later reads), and that it does not exist on v1.

quotes: The API also returns a linked ZPA tenant identifier (`zpaId`)
the API populates `zpaId` lazily (the create response omits it but later GETs include it)
`zpa_id` does not exist on v1 and stays empty on the data source.

metadata-semantics.title: What active, guid and the audit fields guarantee
metadata-semantics.detail: Unverified legacy statements: inactive trusted networks still appear in list responses and must be filtered client-side; `guid` is a stable UUID that survives a rename and is the preferred durable reference; null and empty-string criteria are both ignored, a null or empty criterion is not "match nothing". No source states any of these.

condition-type-values.title: Which trusted network conditionType code is All and which Any
condition-type-values.detail: The Terraform provider maps v1 0 to ALL and 1 to ANY and says it field-verified this against v2's ALL/ANY strings on one tenant ([[zcc.terraform.trusted-network-backend:v1-condition-type-mapping]]). No vendor document gives the codes. The provider documents the forwarding profile's own `conditionType` the other way round (0 ANY, 1 ALL), so the two must not be assumed to share an encoding. A recorded v1 listing carries both codes as JSON numbers, and the network an SDK test created without a `conditionType` (tests-trusted-network-vcr0001) is listed with 0 (one test tenant, recorded with SDK 1.9.13 (Python SDK cassette)); neither says which code is All.
condition-type-values.blocks: saying from raw v1 data whether a trusted network needs all of its criteria
